result.title: EGiME: Entropy-Guided Model Evaluation in Few-Shot Learning
result.summary: The feature-extraction quality of pre-trained models sets the ceiling of downstream transfer learning, yet few-shot model selection remains difficult: supervised evaluation on scarce labels is unstable and yields fluctuating rankings. We propose Entropy-Guided Model Evaluation (EGiME), a semi-supervised criterion that assesses a candidate model from the clustering structure of its feature space without any classifier training. EGiME performs $K$-means clustering over all labeled and unlabeled samples, then combines two entropy terms: an inter-cluster entropy measuring global separability, and an intra-cluster entropy measuring the compactness of labeled anchors, fused through an inverse-frequency weight that emphasizes small clusters. On five few-shot benchmarks and nine pre-trained models, EGiME achieves a correlation score of 0.966 with the full-pool ground-truth accuracy obtained by averaging the accuracies of K-means, KNN, and SVM. At labeling ratios of 4\%--20\%, it produces markedly more stable model rankings than cross-validated supervised baselines, establishing it as a practical alternative to conventional supervised evaluation for pre-trained model selection under data scarcity.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EGiME 这一半监督模型评估准则：对候选预训练模型的特征空间做 K-means，融合簇间熵（全局可分性）与簇内熵（有标签锚点的紧致性）并加权打分，无需训练分类器，在五个 few-shot 基准、九个模型上检验其与真实精度的相关性和排序稳定性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「免标签、依据特征空间聚类结构打分」的思路可能可供核查为 LVR 中 latent 状态是否保留可分视觉证据的代理指标，但论文不涉及推理期状态生成，迁移需较多改造。
